messages:
Sam (AcmeApps): Hey team - we started seeing a bunch of 429s around 11:30 UTC during a short marketing push. App is on the hosted API, single API key, not hitting steady quota but had a brief spike. Docs mention burst credits — can someone explain why we still got throttled?

Maya (Support): Sorry about that, Sam. Can you paste a couple of example request IDs or timestamps and which endpoint you were hitting (generation vs embeddings)? Also roughly how long the spike lasted and RPS numbers if you have them.

Sam (AcmeApps): Sure — it was /v1/generate mostly, spike was ~45s of high traffic, peak ~120 req/s, average during spike ~80 req/s. One request id: req_01GXa2bN. We saw 429 body: "rate_limit_exceeded" and header x-burst-credits-left: 0. We expected burst credits to cover short spikes.

Maya (Support): Thanks. A couple quick checks: 1) can you confirm the API key in the logs is the same key attached to your org quota? 2) did you have any other worker processes sharing the same key?

Sam (AcmeApps): Confirmed single key. No extra workers. Our SDK was doing immediate retries (no jitter/backoff) for 429s — maybe that made things worse.

Ion (SRE): Hey — quick overview: hosted service has two relevant controls: steady quota (tokens/sec or requests/min) and burst credits which are a short-term allowance that replenish slowly. Burst credits are intended to smooth brief spikes but are consumed rapidly for high concurrency. If your peak used all credits in ~10s then subsequent requests hit the steady quota and get 429s. Also worth noting token accounting vs req counting: very long prompts can exhaust more budget per request.

Sam (AcmeApps): Do you have the exact refill window/rate? Docs are a bit vague. We were expecting credits to regen fast enough between spikes.

Ion (SRE): For hosted default accounts, burst credits regenerate at ~4% of max credits per minute (varies by tier). Practically that means a large spike >30RPS sustained for >30s will deplete the bucket and you'll see failures until it recovers. We can look up your org's exact numbers if you want.

Maya (Support): Also a note on client behavior: immediate retry loops without exponential backoff can create a retry storm that prevents recovery. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a max retry cap. Example pseudo from our SDK: 

```js
// basic backoff suggestion
let attempts = 0;
async function callWithBackoff() {
  while (attempts < 6) {
    let res = await callApi();
    if (res.status !== 429) return res;
    attempts++;
    await sleep(Math.pow(2, attempts) * 100 + jitter());
  }
  throw new Error('max retries');
}
```

Priya (Billing): From billing side: burst credits are not billed separately for hosted — they’re part of quota smoothing. You won’t see a direct charge labelled "burst credits"; you’ll just be charged for tokens used. If the spike pushes you above committed reserved capacity, that can affect billing. We can confirm whether any automatic overage billing occurred during that window.

Sam (AcmeApps): No unexpected charges yet — just worried about user errors. Would enabling 'smoothing policy: aggressive' help? I saw a console setting but not sure of tradeoffs.

Ion (SRE): Console smoothing toggles are mainly client-side heuristics we provide for SDKs to limit concurrency on the client before sending. They help a lot for bursty clients. Server-side smoothing is fixed per tier but we offer per-customer tuning for Dedicated plans. For hosted customers we can enable conservative rate limiting headers and raise alerting thresholds for your org temporarily while you ramp.

Maya (Support): To triage: can you run 2 quick repros for us? 1) a small shape test: 60s run at 50 RPS with 1k token prompts. 2) spike test: 20s at 120 RPS with same prompts. Send us the curl and SDK logs. Example curl we used for debugging: 

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b", "input":"short prompt", "max_tokens":256}'
```

Sam (AcmeApps): Will run both in staging and paste logs. Quick Q: those x-burst-credits-* headers — are they reliable? We saw x-burst-credits-left: 0 but no header telling us recharge ETA.

Ion (SRE): Headers include x-burst-credits-left and x-quota-reset-seconds (for steady quota). We don't currently expose an ETA for full recharge because the refill is continuous. But you can estimate: if header says 0 and your max credits is C and refill rate R credits/sec, ETA to full ~ C/R. We'll pull your C & R and add to the incident notes.

ratebot: [system] snapshot for org AcmeApps: 2027-05-12T11:30:12Z spike window detected. burst_credits_start: 320, burst_consumed: 320, steady_quota_limit: 60 rps, regen_rate: 0.1 credits/s.

Maya (Support): Thanks ratebot. Sam — with regen_rate 0.1/s and start 320 that matches ~53m to fully refill, but partial recovery to avoid 429s is much faster. For short-term mitigation: 1) add client-side concurrency cap (eg 30 RPS) 2) use exponential backoff + jitter 3) request temporary quota bump for the time of the campaign or move to Dedicated for predictable throughput.

Sam (AcmeApps): Ok that explains a lot. Two follow-ups: a) can we get a short-lived quota bump for today while we finish the campaign? b) any server-side configuration to reduce the chance of retry storms (e.g., 429 bodies that include retry-after)?

Maya (Support): a) I'll escalate to Product Ops for a temporary bump — need your org id and campaign window. b) we do include Retry-After when available; if header absent use exponential backoff. Also we can flip on more conservative Retry-After behavior for your org (adds a 1–3s server-imposed pause) while you ramp.

Priya (Billing): For temporary bump: if it results in overage beyond your seat/committed capacity, billing will follow your overage terms; we'll notify you. We can also set spend alerts to avoid surprises.

Ion (SRE): After you paste the staging repro logs, we'll simulate your traffic pattern from our end in a traffic-shadow test to validate the fixes (client backoff + concurrency cap). That should reproduce the 429s if the app is the same.

Sam (AcmeApps): Posting logs now. Will also add our org id: org_09876. Campaign window: today 11:15–12:15 UTC. Appreciate the help.

Maya (Support): Got the logs, we see the same request id. Escalating for temporary bump and enabling conservative Retry-After for org_09876. SRE will run the shadow test.

Ion (SRE): Running shadow test now, will post findings in this thread.

[~30m later]

Ion (SRE): Shadow test results: reproduced 429s on the second half of the 20s spike test when client retried aggressively. With an added 25 RPS client-side cap + 200ms jitter/backoff, spike test completed with <1% 429s. Evidence attached in logs (omitted here).

Maya (Support): Temporary bump approved for org_09876 for 1 hour (11:15–12:15 UTC). Conservative Retry-After enabled. Priya will follow up on billing note.

Priya (Billing): Confirmed: no unexpected automatic overage billing during the window; temporary bump will follow team approval and any estimated overage will be communicated.

Sam (AcmeApps): Thanks team — we'll roll the client fix (backoff + cap) immediately and monitor. Appreciate the temporary bump.

Maya (Support): Great. I'll mark this thread resolved after 24h if no further issues. Reopen anytime. :thumbsup:
